activities.caption: place the marker — how wide was the demos?
activities.name: grDemosPlace

config.prompt: What share of Attica's inhabitants could participate — the adult male citizens? Place the marker:
config.why: Perhaps 10–15% of Attica's maybe 250,000–300,000 inhabitants. Women, enslaved people (perhaps a third of the population) and resident foreigners (metics) were outside the demos entirely — democracy and a slave society at once, the paradox every later democracy inherited and re-fought.

activities.caption: file each fact — the machinery or the excluded
activities.name: grLotBuckets

config.prompt: Athenian democracy, up close — file each fact:

items.label: the Council of 500, chosen annually by lot to set the Assembly's agenda
juries of 201, 501 or more — no professional judge; the verdict was the people
ostracism: an annual vote to exile the most dangerous politician for ten years
enslaved people — perhaps a third of Attica

config.why: The lot aimed at one design goal — no permanent political class. Elections, the Athenians suspected, would quietly restore aristocracy: the famous, well-off and well-spoken winning by default.

activities.anchor: Democracy created the questions and the thinkers
activities.caption: pair each thinker with his answer
activities.name: grThinkersMatch

config.prompt: The polis as laboratory — pair each thinker with his answer:

pairs.right: made argument itself a civic act — executed by an Athenian jury in 399 BCE, officially for impiety
rule by the knowledgeable — philosopher-kings, written partly in grief at the democracy that killed his teacher
studied 158 constitutions and sorted regimes by who rules and for whom
the first analytic history — power, fear and hubris examined clinically in the Peloponnesian War

config.why: The trio fixed the vocabulary — politics, constitution, citizenship, tyranny — that every later debate runs in.

activities.anchor: Rome's constitution was unwritten and grew like a coral
activities.caption: line up the republic's breakdown, earliest first
activities.name: grRepublicOrder

config.prompt: The republic that could not scale — order the breakdown, earliest first:
items: the Gracchi brothers' reform attempts end in political murder — 133 and 123 BCE
a century of civil war: Marius and Sulla
Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon — 49 BCE
Augustus' principate — monarchy in republican dress, holding army, treasury and grain supply
config.why: Institutions designed for a city-state could not digest an empire: generals with provincial armies became more loyal to their troops than to the Senate, and land concentration displaced smallholders. The pax Romana then worked for two centuries.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the law that outlived the empire
activities.name: grLawCloze

config.text: The %%0%% (c. 450 BCE) made law a public text posted in the Forum; in %%1%% the emperor Caracalla extended citizenship to nearly all free inhabitants; and Justinian's %%2%% — rediscovered in medieval Bologna's law schools from about %%3%% — became the skeleton of the civil-law systems.
config.hint: Law as shared text rather than privileged knowledge — innocent until proven guilty carries the tradition into most modern civil-law systems.

activities.anchor: the Pont du Gard still stands 49 m high
activities.caption: call the volume — water by gravity alone
activities.name: grWaterEstimate

config.prompt: Rome's eleven aqueducts delivered roughly how much water to the city daily?
config.why: Perhaps a million cubic metres daily, moved by gravity alone — channels dropping centimetres per hundred metres over tens of kilometres, through tunnels and on arcades like the Pont du Gard, still standing 49 m high.
config.context: Roughly 80,000 km of paved roads moved legions, post and trade at speeds unmatched until railways.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — slavery, unsentimentally
activities.name: grSlaverySpot

config.prompt: One line of this classical-slavery summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Athens' silver mines of Laurion were worked largely by enslaved people.
Conquest supplied Rome captives by the hundreds of thousands — 150,000 from the sack of Epirus alone (167 BCE).
At the empire's height, Italy's population may have been 10–20% enslaved.
Enslaved people were drawn almost exclusively from Africa, by skin colour.
Manumission was routine and created a large freed class.
config.correction: The ancient institution drew its victims mainly from war, piracy and debt — enslaved people were of every origin and appearance; race-based, lifelong, hereditary chattel slavery is a specific later construction.
config.why: The classics' celebration of liberty was written by societies whose liberty was someone else's labour — the honest account carries both facts in one hand.

activities.caption: drag the divider — fall versus transformation
activities.name: grFallCompare

config.prompt: The 'fall' of 476 is a framing choice — drag the divider between the two cases:

before.label: Ward-Perkins — the fall
before.text: Economic complexity, literacy and taxation contracted sharply in the west — a case built on pottery and cattle-bone archaeology.

after.label: Peter Brown — transformation
after.text: Institutions, language and law blended gradually into the successor kingdoms — change as a spectrum, not a cliff.

config.why: The eastern half — Byzantium — thrived another thousand years, and 'Byzantine' is a modern label coined about a century after that empire died. No single cause: a resilient system absorbing shocks until the shocks compounded.
